- scripts/smoke_review_dispatch.sh:smoke_review_checked_out_sha, around the `log_file="$(mktemp)"` block
  PROBLEM: The temp file created with mktemp is removed only on the explicit return / fall-through paths; if the caller exits abnormally (set -e trap, signal), the file leaks under /tmp.
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: add `trap 'rm -f "${log_file}"' RETURN` immediately after the mktemp call so every return path runs the cleanup.
- scripts/smoke_review_dispatch.sh:smoke_review_pr_named_runs input validation
  PROBLEM: Workflow-file regex `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*\.yml$` allows multiple consecutive dots in the basename (e.g. `a..b.yml`), producing a syntactically valid but almost certainly 404 path on the API.
  WHY: Suggested minimal fix: tighten the middle character class to disallow adjacent dots, e.g. `^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)*\\.yml$`, so the bash side fails closed before the API round-trip.

- scripts/smoke_review_dispatch.sh:`grep -aE '^[^[:space:]]+ Captured INITIAL_HEAD_SHA=[0-9a-f]{40} for stale-base detection\.$'` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The grep pattern only matches lowercase hexadecimal SHAs (`[0-9a-f]{40}`), but the workflow comparison uses case-insensitive matching (`${BAIT_SHA,,}` and `${RETRY_DISPATCH_SHA,,}`). If the Actions log contains an uppercase SHA, the grep will not match and the function returns 2 (line not found), causing verification to fail.
  WHY: Git SHAs can be represented in either case. The test fixtures use lowercase SHAs (`BAIT = "b" * 40`), but there is no test covering uppercase SHAs in the log. The workflow's case-insensitive comparison suggests the code is prepared for either case, but the grep pattern is case-sensitive, creating a mismatch that could cause false negatives.
